title: Webb Telescope Captures the First Stellar Merger of Its Kind! ✨
body: Webb Telescope Captures the First Stellar Merger of Its Kind! ✨

For the first time in history, scientists have observed two stars merging in a way never seen before: a small star, roughly the size of our Sun, was pulled toward a giant, bloated star in the Andromeda galaxy, orbited it just seven times, and was then swallowed by it.
A stellar merger means two stars collide and become a single star — a rare event that helps scientists understand how stars live and die.

The James Webb Space Telescope observed the event just 47 days after the peak of its explosion — the fastest follow-up of its kind ever. The large star has a mass 7 times that of the Sun, a diameter 350 times greater, and a brightness 18,000 times greater, while the small star is about 0.7 solar masses.
Did you ever imagine a star swallowing another star? 🌟
